summary: gc removes a clean, merged worktree with `worktree remove --force`, then `rm -rf` if it stays, then `worktree prune`; a failure prints `! could not remove <wt>: <why>` and the loop goes on; --dry-run prints `would: … --force` for each. Two new checks (watched red first); the loop never touches the project's own checkout. 309 → 311 checks.
verified_how: bash tests/run.sh before the fix: 309/311 (both new checks FAIL); after: 311/311 via lib/check.sh (green in 526 s); bash -n bin/harness and tests/run.sh

discoveries.text: A worktree whose parent is read-only: `git worktree remove --force` empties it, removes its .git file and fails with `error: failed to delete '<wt>': Permission denied`; rm -rf then fails too; after `worktree prune` git no longer lists it, so the branch pass can still delete its branch. gc's worktree loop now skips the project checkout ($wt == $p) explicitly, since rm -rf follows a failed remove.
tests/run.sh has gw_add/gw_listed helpers and $T/proj/.git/info/exclude now lists .next/ (L4-02 block after the L4-01 branch checks); the gcw-* worktrees and branches are cleaned up after.
